posts.text:
Most people assume SpaceX began because Elon Musk wanted to build rockets, but the original idea was smaller. 

Around 2001 he looked for the date of NASA's Mars mission, discovered there were no plans to send people at all, and came up with Mars Oasis, a little greenhouse with seeds in dehydrated gel that would land on Mars and send back an image of green plants against red soil, just to get people excited about space again and help NASA get a bigger budget. 

Then he realized the real obstacle was the cost of rockets: "I was wrong… there actually was plenty of will if people thought there was a way. So then I decided, okay, well, I need to work on the way." 

SpaceX was born to serve the dream of exploration, not to compete with it 🩵

Tesla VP of Vehicle Engineering Lars Moravy just put Tesla's extraordinary manufacturing scale into perspective during his conversation with Jay Leno

“You know, a lot of people don't realize that Tesla is the largest selling luxury vehicle in the world now”

And the numbers behind Tesla's growth are absolutely staggering

Tesla has now manufactured over 10 MILLION electric vehicles worldwide

Just look at the progress:

• July 2026: 10 million vehicles

Tesla went from its first million vehicles to 10 million in just six years

When Tesla crossed the milestone, the company celebrated:

From proving electric vehicles could compete with combustion-engine cars to manufacturing millions of them across factories in the United States, China, and Germany

A battery cost $600 per kilowatt-hour. The materials it’s made of, according to Elon Musk, cost about $80.

REPORTER: Where does that gap come from?

ELON MUSK: Most people reason by analogy. They say batteries will always be expensive because they’ve always been expensive. That’s pretty dumb.

REPORTER: Why?

ELON MUSK: If you applied that reasoning to anything new, you’d never get to the new thing. You can’t say, “Horses are great, we’re used to them, and there’s no gasoline to buy, so nobody will ever want a car.” And people did say that.

REPORTER: So how should you reason?

ELON MUSK: From first principles, not by analogy. Normally we do something because it’s like something that was done before, or because other people are doing it.

REPORTER: What are first principles?

ELON MUSK: The physics way of looking at the world. You boil things down to the most fundamental truths and reason up from there.

REPORTER: Why doesn’t everyone do that?

ELON MUSK: Because it takes a lot more mental energy.

REPORTER: Can you give an example?

ELON MUSK: Batteries. Historically it’s $600 per kilowatt-hour, and they say it won’t get much better. I ask something else: what is it made of?

REPORTER: And what is it made of?

ELON MUSK: Cobalt, nickel, aluminum, carbon, some polymers for separation, and a sealed can.

REPORTER: And what does that cost?

ELON MUSK: At London Metal Exchange prices it comes to something like $80 per kilowatt-hour.

REPORTER: So that’s almost eight times less. What do you do with that?

ELON MUSK: Come up with clever ways to combine those materials into the shape of a battery cell. And then batteries can be much cheaper than anyone realizes.

quote.author: ThayzzySmith
quote.name: Conservatism And Elegance 🇺🇲
quote.text:
ELON MUSK: “A conta de luz da IA é alta demais? Então, basta construir um data center no espaço”

“Em vez de economizar energia na Terra, a ideia de se mudar para o espaço”

REPÓRTER: “A IA consome uma quantidade absurda de eletricidade, né?”

ELON MUSK: “É verdade.”

REPÓRTER: “E isso vai aumentar ainda mais no futuro?”

ELON MUSK: “Se a IA evoluir, a demanda por energia também vai crescer, provavelmente.”

REPÓRTER: “Então a conta de luz vai ser um problemão!”

ELON MUSK: “Por isso vamos usar o espaço.”

REPÓRTER: “.... Hein?”

ELON MUSK: “Vamos construir um data center para IA no espaço.”

REPÓRTER: “Peraí, a gente tava falando de conta de luz, cara”

ELON MUSK: “E é exatamente isso que eu tô respondendo.”

REPÓRTER: “Por que raios no espaço, mano?!”

ELON MUSK: “Porque dá pra usar energia solar.”

REPÓRTER: “Energia solar a gente já usa aqui na Terra, né?”

ELON MUSK: “Mas na Terra tem noite, não tem?”

REPÓRTER: “É, tem sim.”

ELON MUSK: “E a geração varia por causa do clima.”

REPÓRTER: “Hmm, entendi.”

ELON MUSK: “No espaço, ajustando a órbita, dá pra captar luz solar por muito mais tempo.”

REPÓRTER: “Então você vai colocar painéis solares no espaço?”

ELON MUSK: “Exatamente isso.”

REPÓRTER: “Mas os computadores da IA não esquentam pra caramba?”

ELON MUSK: “Claro que geram calor.”

REPÓRTER: “No espaço não tem ar-condicionado, né?”

ELON MUSK: “A gente usa dispositivos de dissipação de calor.”

REPÓRTER: “Dispositivos de dissipação?”

ELON MUSK: “Os painéis solares ficam virados pro Sol.”

REPÓRTER: “Tá.”

ELON MUSK: “Do lado oposto, colocamos equipamentos que liberam o calor pro vácuo do espaço.”

REPÓRTER: “Entendi!”

ELON MUSK: “É a radiação do calor pro espaço sideral.”

REPÓRTER: “Então o resfriamento é de graça!?”

ELON MUSK: “Não, ainda precisa de equipamentos.”

REPÓRTER: “Que é que é isso?”

ELON MUSK: “Mas dá pra criar um sistema bem mais eficiente.”

REPÓRTER: “E aí, pra quando isso rola?”

ELON MUSK: “Em 2 ou 3 anos, acho que o espaço vai ser o lugar mais barato pra rodar IA.”

REPÓRTER: “... 2 ou 3 anos!?”

ELON: “É o que eu prevejo.”

REPÓRTER: “Rápido demais, cara”

ELON MUSK: “O progresso da tecnologia é acelerado.”

REPÓRTER: “Mas pra levar tudo de foguete, gasta uma grana preta!”

ELON MUSK: “É aí que tá o pulo do gato.”

REPÓRTER: “Como assim?”

ELON MUSK: “Precisa reduzir drasticamente o custo de lançamento.”

REPÓRTER: “Ah, sei...”

ELON MUSK: “Se o transporte pro espaço ficar barato, as opções se abrem.”

REPÓRTER: “Ou seja, foguetes e IA tão todos interligados!?”

ELON MUSK: “É nesse futuro que eu tô pensando.”

REPÓRTER: “Cara, essa visão já não é de humano da Terra”

ELON MUSK: “Tem possibilidades fora da Terra também.”

Musk to Texas Democrats: Our Success Came From Freedom, Not Your Favors

Elon Musk just slapped down a Wall Street Journal story claiming Texas Democrats plan to yank the "white-glove treatment" for SpaceX and Tesla now that they've flipped the state. He made it plain: the companies thrived here because the government stayed out of the way.

"SpaceX and Tesla have prospered in Texas, because we were not constantly operating under an oppressive and extractive state government," Musk wrote.

He explained the practical reasons too. Factories need hands-on leadership. "And I need to be close to the factories, so that I can walk the floor in person. That’s why the first major SpaceX factory was in LA and first major Tesla factory was in SF Bay Area."

Then California turned hostile. "As California became increasingly difficult, due to extreme taxes and overregulation, we moved our major domestic expansions and HQ to Texas."

This is the same pattern that hollowed out California's tech and manufacturing base. High taxes, endless rules, and politicians treating productive companies like piñatas drove the growth elsewhere. Texas offered the opposite: lower burdens, faster permitting, and room to build. Jobs followed. Investment followed. Rockets and cars got built instead of lawsuits.

Now the new Democratic leadership is signaling they want to change the deal. They talk about ending special treatment, scrutinizing land deals, slowing data centers, and reviewing incentives. Translation: they see a successful employer and reach for the regulatory toolbox. The same approach that chased SpaceX and Tesla out of California is being imported to Texas.

Musk is not asking for favors. He is stating the obvious. Companies locate where they can operate without constant extraction and interference. Texas gained by being less California. If Democrats reverse that, the next expansion, the next factory, the next launch complex will simply go somewhere else. Florida has already been mentioned. Other red states are open for business.

The left celebrates the blue wave as a rebuke to Musk's spending. What they are actually celebrating is the chance to punish the companies that create the jobs and tax base they want to spend. History shows how that ends. California wrote the playbook. Texas is now being invited to copy it.
